subject.title: [Bug] web_search tool returns "DuckDuckGo search failed: query is mandatory" despite valid query input

question: If live evidence confirms Ollama receives a valid query yet returns this DuckDuckGo-derived error, should OpenClaw retain fail-fast Ollama-provider errors, normalize this known upstream failure, or add an explicitly configured fallback path?
rationale: The source and docs establish the route but not the error origin; choosing cross-provider retry or an error-contract change affects explicit provider selection and user expectations.

options.title: Require live trace first
options.body: Collect a redacted failing request/response pair and decide ownership from evidence before changing routing or fallback behavior.

options.title: Document upstream limitation
options.body: If Ollama confirms this is its service behavior, document the limitation and recommended alternative provider without changing runtime routing.

options.title: Design opt-in fallback
options.body: If maintainers want resilience beyond the current provider contract, specify an explicit configured fallback design with compatibility tests.

recommendation.title: Require live trace first
recommendation.body: Collect a redacted failing request/response pair and decide ownership from evidence before changing routing or fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Current provider-routing and Ollama web-search history most strongly connects this area to `steipete`.
